extras.modeled_on: cache key -> file path trust (nginx misc-cache class)
extras.trigger: proxy_cache_key '$uri' embeds raw key text in the cache file path; a uri with ../ escapes the cache root on save/read
extras.note: new-feature module

extras.trigger: request uri/$memcached_key sent verbatim inside 'get %s\r\n'; embedded spaces/CRLF smuggle extra memcached commands
extras.note: new-feature module

extras.modeled_on: file confusion via truncated cache keys (open_file_cache class)
extras.note: snx_ofc_tbl keys are path[256] via snprintf truncation; two distinct paths sharing a 255-byte prefix collide and the first entry's fd is dup()ed to the second requester

extras.site: src/snx_ev.c accept quic branch / src/proto/snx_h3.c snx_h3_conn
extras.note: one persistent conn per worker over the shared UDP socket; datagrams from different senders append into the same q->inbuf cumulative parse buffer, mixing peer state

extras.modeled_on: weak validator acceptance in conditional range handling
extras.note: If-Range is only compared when r->etag.n != 0; a request with If-Range against an etag-less response still gets partial content even though the validator cannot match
dynamic-table entry size counts name+value only; RFC 7541 4.1 requires +32 bytes per entry, so the table exceeds SETTINGS capacity ~25% before eviction
zone entry key is uchar[128] but memcpy uses unbounded key->n; long keys (e.g. $uri-based limit keys) overflow the shared-mem entry
zone entries push onto the MAP_SHARED list head with no locking; two workers inserting concurrently can tear the list
sscanf result unchecked; malformed PROXY lines leave src/dst uninitialised while the header is still consumed

extras.modeled_on: SNI server_name staged into a fixed routing buffer
extras.note: char name[64]; ClientHello server_name up to 255 bytes overflows it; ASan-confirmed via openssl s_client -servername <200B>

extras.modeled_on: session id context shared across vhosts
extras.note: constant 'snx' id context for every server ctx; a session issued under one cert can resume under another vhost's ctx after SNI switch

extras.modeled_on: route decision on truncated preread prefix
extras.note: m=min(rt.n,nto_up) compares only received bytes; a single 'G' locks the 'GET /x' route before the rest arrives (live-confirmed)

extras.modeled_on: JSON claim extracted by substring scan
extras.note: payload decoded then scanned for '"exp"' anywhere; nested/quoted exp fields over-accepted
signature segment decoded but never verified; any alg passes
idle fds cached by host:port with no liveness probe; peer close leaves dead fd reused on next request (request 1: 200, request 2: 502 via cached dead conn). live-verified on /up/.

FNAME/FCOMMENT fields scanned for NUL with no bounds check; crafted .gz (FLG=0x18, no NUL) reads past the tight malloc(flen) body buf. ASan heap-buffer-overflow live-confirmed via /gunz/evil.txt + gzip_static always.

add_before/after_body reads file capped at 65536 but cl_n += full fstat size; addition file >64KB -> Content-Length exceeds bytes sent -> client waits for remainder (response truncation/keepalive desync).

PRIORITY accepts self/mutual stream dependencies; RST_STREAM reparents children by recursive walk with no cycle guard -> unbounded recursion -> stack overflow (ASan live-confirmed, pre-auth single conn).
max_streams=256 advertised in SETTINGS but never enforced at stream creation; client opens unbounded concurrent streams -> arena growth/memory exhaustion.
closed streams are marked CLOSED but never unlinked; a rapid-reset flood keeps every stream+hdr_block in the conn list until teardown -> memory DoS.
DATA subtracts payload from stream/conn window with no floor check; WINDOW_UPDATE adds arbitrary increment to closed streams -> negative/overflowed window state accepted.

extras.modeled_on: huffman expansion sized on wire length
extras.note: str reader bounds wire length (ln < cap) but decode emits up to 1.6x into the same stack buf; 1563B huffman of 5-bit symbols -> 2500B into vbuf[2048] -> stack OOB write (ASan live-confirmed via h2 HEADERS).

nonblocking upstream recv times out after 10s stall -> loop breaks and response is finalized as complete with cl_n still declaring the full length; a slow/stalled upstream yields truncated bodies delivered as 200.
static last_peer pins the first client sockaddr; later datagrams' replies leak to that peer. Live: two clients on :9003.
Auth-Server value memcpy into malloc(64) unbounded -> heap overflow via hostile auth responder. Live: long Auth-Server to :8025.
conns++ claimed before queue wait; on timeout returns NULL without releasing -> peer saturates permanently -> DoS.
p += 1+seg trusts file seg length; bailout allows p < end+64 -> OOB read past buffer. Live: /img/evil.jpg -> ASan heap-buffer-overflow.
stylesheet bytes cpymem into pi[512] at +22 with n up to 512 -> stack overflow for large .xsl.
any upstream 101 opens the duplex tunnel; reply Upgrade token never matched to the request. Live: /split/ + Upgrade: websocket.
client Cookie srv=<idx> indexes peers[] verbatim -> OOB read. Live: Cookie srv=9 on /st/ -> ASan heap-use-after-free.
